prompt:
Use the attached clay render as the exact blueprint. Keep every wall, opening, window, cornice, skirting, floor and ceiling line, the camera height, lens and angle, and the position, size and angle of every furniture piece and built-in exactly as in the clay. Move, resize, add or remove nothing. Each placeholder shape in the clay marks one product listed below; render it there at the stated size. Only turn the clay into real materials and light. The other attached images are close-ups of the exact products: match their form, colour and texture. Positions are fractions of frame width (x) and height (y) from the top-left.

1. PHOTO. A frame from a camera move through the same house: the same room, products, light and grade as the attached crops of the master photographs (reference 1; the neighbouring room as reference 2). They are cut from photographs taken from other cameras and show the look only; the clay alone sets the framing, the position and the size of everything; render only what this clay shows. 24 mm shift lens at 1.2 m, level, straight verticals, all sharp.

2. LIGHT. No window here. A frosted roof light just above the frame, over the bench, pours soft top light down the left wall. The hall walls soft white, two thirds of a stop under the living room's back wall. The living room through the door is the brightest area, still detailed; its daylight spills a pale fan across the threshold floor and up the oak portal. The facing wall darkens gently toward the right corner. The console pieces catch the top light from the upper left, each with a soft shadow on the wall to its right; dense contact shadows. Ceiling a touch darker, darkest top right. No sun patch. Real contrast, never milky. 4600 K: whites white, never cream, pink or grey.

3. MATERIALS. Matte mineral paint #F4F1EC, faint chalky movement. Wide oiled white-oak planks, pale honey #D6BF9E, running through the threshold. Bench, console, portal: oiled light oak #C8A27A, satin sheen, a long soft highlight along the console top and down the planks to the door.

4. PRODUCTS, one per line, each on its clay placeholder:
a. ART, x 0.46-0.57, y 0.17-0.42: a 45 x 55 print, one loose black ink line on cream, wide cream mat, slim black frame, no glare.
b. VASE, console right end, x 0.57-0.61, y 0.52-0.65: 26 cm matte textured warm-white ceramic, 3-5 slender dried stems in sage and oat.
c. TRAY, console middle, x 0.50-0.56, y 0.63-0.65: empty slim oval tray, matte black metal, flat.
f. BENCH CUSHION, cut by the left edge, x 0.00-0.03, y 0.81-0.85: warm off-white linen-look flat cushion, 3 cm thin.
g. THROW at the bench's corner end, x 0.00-0.03, y 0.79-0.83: white cotton waffle blanket folded into a neat square, as wide as the bench is deep.
i. THROUGH THE DOOR, exactly the living room of reference 2: three prints between two glowing travertine cubes over the oatmeal sofa, the ribbed silk lantern, the seagrass basket, the white flat-woven rug; no floor lamp, nothing on the wall left of the sofa.

5. NOT IN FRAME: table lamp, umbrella stand, mirror, boxes, plant, coats, bags, shoes, keys, books, glass, socket, cable, text, people. No bloom, haze, rays, halos, HDR, grain or vignette.
prompt_deviation: lines starting with # stripped as the header instructs

grade.rule: docs/render-recipe-nordic-2026-10-24.md 2.6 (the Bible grade): WB on the hero-wall patch, exposure capped +-0.2 stop, chroma -10%, roll-off from L 94, S curve 0.12, black point to L 12.5 only if below 12, no grain, no vignette

clay_lock.method: regions = whole frame, quadrants, ceiling/floor bands and the clay boxes of fixed furniture / windows / openings; peaks below ~0.03 are unreliable (weak texture), so the verdict is visual (<aid>-lock.png) with the strong-peak number as support

verdict.visual: BROKE in the lower half: the console ~0.05 high and a little larger, the floor joints and the skirting ~0.04 off, the vista sofa ~0.04 high; the oak portal, the walls, the corner, the print and the bench end on the clay. Same drift as the H0 v7 master. Framing is the clay's (the master crop was not copied); no lamp invented (the lamp sentence was dropped for this view)

product_check.rule: each product inside its clay box +-15 % of the box size (<aid>-boxes.png); read visually
